headline: The European Union's technology chief, Henna Virkkunen, said Europe is "well equipped" to handle rogue AI agents under its AI Act.
score_reason: Kept at the pool score: a senior official's on-record position, but it is her own assessment of her own law and no action follows.
importance_line: It tells AI developers and EU citizens that Brussels sees its existing AI Act as enough to handle rogue AI, though this is one official's view.
summary: Reuters reports that Henna Virkkunen, the European Commission's tech chief, said in an interview on 9 Oct that the AI Act, the EU's risk-based AI law adopted two years ago, covers "the whole life cycle" of advanced models and that regulators will draw on a 60-member panel of scientific experts. In late August the Commission sent information requests to AI companies about their safety practices; this is an official's own assessment, not a ruling.
notes: Reuters blocked (401); read The News International relay and Cryptopolitan. Attribution to Reuters rests on the matching Reuters headline and the same quotes.
